summary: Disused fire lookout on Paget Peak in Yoho National Park, reached by a 3.5 km day hike; a travel blog dates it to 1944, Wikipedia only to after the early-1940s fires.

access.note: Listed among Parks Canada day hikes. The listing mentions no closure.

visit.trail_note: 3.5 km one way from the Sherbrooke Lake parking lot; the trailhead can be reached from Highway 1 westbound only.

events.note: Given by one travel blog only. Wikipedia dates the lookout to after the serious fires of the late 1930s and early 1940s, with no year.

evidence.supports: Parks Canada describes the trail as leading to an old fire lookout
evidence.quote: Steep, rocky trail to an old fire lookout with stunning views of the Bow, Cataract Brook, and Kicking Horse valleys.

evidence.supports: Climbing of 525 m on the route
evidence.quote: Elevation gain: 525 m | Elevation loss: 15 m

evidence.supports: Estimated return time of three hours
Trailhead at Sherbrooke Lake parking lot; westbound access only
evidence.quote: Trailhead: Sherbrooke Lake parking lot on the north side of the Trans-Canada Highway, 11 km east of Field, B.C. Highway 1 westbound access only.

evidence.supports: Built after serious fires in the late 1930s and early 1940s; used until the late 1970s
evidence.quote: The lookout was built after two seasons of serious forest fires in the late 1930s and early 1940s, and was used until the late 1970s.

evidence.supports: Wikipedia calls it one of the first built in the park; disused today
evidence.quote: This is a hiking trail that leads to a disused fire lookout on the southern slope, one of the first to be built in the park.

evidence.supports: Blog gives 1944 as the build year and calls it the oldest surviving fire lookout in the national parks
evidence.quote: Built in 1944, Mount Paget Lookout is the oldest surviving fire lookout in the national parks.

evidence.supports: Blog says the lookout was manned May to September and that by the 1970s air patrols and satellite sensing were used to detect fires
evidence.quote: It was manned from May to September and by the 1970’s, air patrols and satellite remote sensing were used to detect fires.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia calls the lookout one of the first built in the park. The travel blog calls it the oldest surviving fire lookout in the national parks. The story gives both and attributes each.

sources.title: Day hikes in Yoho National Park
Why Paget Peak Is The Best Scramble In Yoho

notes_for_editor: The 1944 build year rests on one travel blog. Wikipedia gives only the fire-season context, and no primary Parks Canada or heritage record was found; a register check could settle the year. The blog and Wikipedia differ on rank (oldest surviving vs one of the first); the story attributes both. The brief's coordinates are an approximate name match to the peak (CGNDB), not the lookout's own position. The brief's agency (Parks Canada) is supported by the Parks Canada page. Other blog details (interior, condition) were left out as unverified.
